data.text:
You are scouting for OPENLY LICENSED, de-identified judgment-and-decision-making datasets that could support a secondary analysis, and for large open datasets usable to validate a decision-making simulation. Constraint: no personal identifiers; license must permit research reuse (CC0, CC-BY, MIT, public domain, etc.).

Context: three prior papers used (1) OpAQ anchoring data, (2) Good Judgment Project forecasting data, (3) a simulation. Avoid re-using OpAQ and GJP.

TASK: Find and document at least 8 concrete openly licensed JDM or behavioral-decision datasets. For each, record: name; URL (OSF/Dataverse/Zenodo/GitHub/PsychArchives); license; size (N participants, N trials); what variables exist (especially choice, confidence, response time, framing, risk, intertemporal, advice); a direct download link if possible; and known prior analyses that would affect novelty.

Strong candidates to check specifically (verify they exist and are openly licensed):
- The Confidence Database (Rahnev et al. 2020, Nature Human Behaviour) — OSF, trial-level confidence/accuracy across many tasks. Find the current version and license.
- Choice Prediction Competition data (CPC15/CPC18/CPC2023; Erev, Plonsky et al.) — GitHub / OSF.
- Decisions-from-experience datasets (e.g., Hertwig et al.; Wulff et al.).
- The "Adolescent" / "Baby" decision datasets, Mouselab process-tracing data.
- Open Science Foundation "Many Labs", Psychological Science Accelerator, and any JDM-related replication datasets.
- Risk-preference elicitation datasets (e.g., the "Holt-Laury" replication data; DOBBS; "Risk aversion" datasets).
- "Cognitive Reflection Test" open datasets.
- Any JDM data on OSF search: https://osf.io/search?q=judgment%20decision
- The "Basel" / "SOEP" data if openly licensed and de-identified.

METHOD: Use webfetch/curl. Verify license by fetching the dataset page. Check each dataset's Terms. Do not invent URLs — open each one. Note that OSF pages may need the API: https://api.osf.io/v2/nodes/?filter[title]=...

OUTPUT: Write the full catalog to ~/Documents/Coding/ai-jdm-paper4/scoping/data_catalog.md and return a concise ranked shortlist of the 4 most usable datasets (license, downloadability, JDM relevance, novelty headroom). Be rigorous: mark anything you could not verify as unverified.


=== CPC18 dictionary preview (first bytes) ===
-rw-r--r--@ 1 lukaswallrich  wheel  198794 Sep 28 16:19 cpc18dict.pdf
Dictionary for the variable names in CPC18 raw data
SubjID – Unique human subject identifier, made up of 5 digits. 1st digit marks the Set of games
the subject faced (1-7), 2nd digit marks Location subject played in (0-1), last three digits have no
meaning.
Location – The physical location the subject was run in (“Technion”/“Rehovot”)
Gender – Subject’s gender (M/F)
Age – Subject’s age at time of experiment
Set – ID for the set number that the subject faced (each set consists of the same 30 games). 1-5
are CPC15 data, 6-7 are CPC18’s Experiment 1 data.
Condition – Legacy variable from CPC15 (“ByProb”/”ByFB”). Refers to the order condition by
which subject saw the games within a set. CPC18 data will all be “ByProb” condition.
GameID – Unique game (choice problem) identifier (1-210).
<< The next 12 variables define (jointly) the choice problem by defining the two possible
distributions and any relationship between them. For more details on how each 12-tuple defines
the exact distributions, see the paper >>
Ha – Expected value of (High) lottery in Option A
pHa – Probability to get payoff drawn from lottery in Option A
La – Low payoff in Option A
LotShapeA – Shape of lottery in Option A (“-“, “Symm”, “L-skew”, or “R-skew”)
LotNumA – Number of lottery outcomes in Option A
Hb – Expected value of (High) lottery in Option B
pHb – Probability to get payoff drawn from lottery in Option B
Lb – Low payoff in Option B
LotShapeB – Shape of lottery in Option B (“-“, “Symm”, “L-skew”, or “R-skew”)

 LotNumB – Number of lottery outcomes in Option B
Amb – Whether Option B is ambiguous (i.e. its probabilities are not described to subjects;
Boolean)
Corr – Whether payoffs generated by the two possible options are correlated and the sign
of the correlation (-1/0/1)
Order – The serial position of the current game within the sequence of 30 games the subject
faced (1-30)
Trial – The trial number within a game (1-25)
Button – The on-screen side of the chosen button (“L”/”R”)
B – The response variable. Whether or not the subject selected Option B in the current trial
(Boolean)
Payoff – The payoff the subject got from her/his choice in the current trial
Forgone – The payoff the subject would have gotten had she/he selected the other option in the
current trial
RT – Reaction time until choice of option (in milliseconds). Only measured for Sets 6, 7.
<< The next four variables can be computed directly from the previous variables. They are given
for convenience. >>
APay – The payoff provided by Option A in the current trial
BPay – The payoff provided by Option B in the current trial
Feedback – Whether (full) feedback was provided for the subject regarding payoffs in the current
trial
Block – Number of time-block within the current game (each 5 trials define a block)

 === OSF s46pr contributor / description ===
Database of confidence studies

=== EuropePMC Rahnev Confidence Database ===
TITLE: The Confidence Database.
YEAR: 2020
ABSTRACT: Understanding how people rate their confidence is critical for the characterization of a wide range of perceptual, memory, motor and cognitive processes. To enable the continued exploration of these processes, we created a large database of confidence studies spanning a broad set of paradigms, participant populations and fields of study. The data from each study are structured in a common, easy-to-use format that can be easily imported and analysed using multiple software packages. Each dataset is accompanied by an explanation regarding the nature of the collected data. At the time of publication, the Confidence Database (which is available at https://osf.io/s46pr/) contained 145 datasets with data from more than 8,700 participants and almost 4 million trials. The database will remain open for new submissions indefinitely and is expected to continue to grow. Here we show the usefulness of this large collection of datasets in four different analyses that provide precise estimations of several foundational confidence-related effects.

input.content:
# Openly licensed JDM / behavioural-decision datasets — scoping catalog

Date of scouting: 2026-09-28
Scope: de-identified, openly licensed datasets usable either for (a) a secondary JDM analysis or (b) validation of a decision-making simulation. Excludes OpAQ (anchoring) and Good Judgment Project (forecasting), per brief.
Method: OSF API v2 (`api.osf.io/v2/nodes/`), Zenodo REST API, Crossref, Europe PMC, GitHub API. Every URL below was opened and every license read from the repository's own license field. Anything not confirmed is marked **UNVERIFIED**.

License key: CC0 / CC-BY-4.0 / MIT = fully permissive for research reuse. CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0 = research reuse OK, no commercial use, share-alike. `none` = no license declared → **all rights reserved, do not reuse without written permission** (listed only to document the gap).

---

## A. Verified, openly licensed datasets

### A1. The Confidence Database
- **URL / DOI:** https://osf.io/s46pr/ — OSF DOI `10.17605/OSF.IO/S46PR`
- **Citation:** Rahnev et al. (2020), *The Confidence Database*, Nature Human Behaviour 4, 317–325. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41562-019-0813-1
- **License:** **CC0 1.0 Universal** (verified via OSF license id `563c1cf88c5e4a3877f9e96c`).
- **Size:** At publication: **145 datasets, >8,700 participants, ~4 million trials** (verified from the published abstract). The live OSF storage folder has since grown to **360 files / ~255 MB** (data CSVs + per-study readmes).
- **Variables:** trial-level **confidence rating**, **accuracy/correctness**, and task condition; many studies also carry response time, stimulus parameters, and demographics. Structured in a common format (one CSV + one readme per study).
- **Download:** direct per-file, e.g. https://osf.io/download/xkc7b/ (Database_Information.xlsx); individual study CSVs via the `osfstorage` folder. No registration.
- **Prior analyses / novelty headroom:** The original paper ran four exemplar aggregate analyses. It is a "database" project explicitly designed for reuse, so many secondary papers exist (individual-differences in metacognition, confidence–accuracy calibration, domain generality). **Low licence risk, moderate novelty headroom** — strongest as a large aggregated sample for a *new* question rather than confirming known confidence effects.

### A2. CPC2015 — Raw data (decisions under risk, ambiguity, and from experience)
- **URL / DOI:** https://zenodo.org/records/321652 — `10.5281/zenodo.321652`
- **Citation:** Erev, Ert & Plonsky (2017). CPC2015 choice prediction competition.
- **License:** **CC-BY-4.0** (verified via Zenodo API).
- **Size:** **>330,000 consequential choices** between two prospects; 3 experiment files (7 MB, 9 MB, 10 MB CSV) ≈ 26 MB.
- **Variables:** participant ID, location/gender/age, choice problem (two lotteries: outcomes × probabilities), condition (by-probability vs by-feedback / description vs experience), trial, **choice** (B), payoff, forgone payoff, block; **RT only in a subset**.
- **Download (direct):**
  - https://zenodo.org/records/321652/files/RawDataExperiment1sorted.csv/content
  - https://zenodo.org/records/321652/files/RawDataExperiment2sorted.csv/content
  - https://zenodo.org/records/321652/files/RawDataExperiment3sorted.csv/content
- **Prior analyses / novelty headroom:** Competition papers (Erev et al. 2010, 2017) and follow-up modelling papers. Substantially less re-analysed than CPC18 → **good novelty headroom**.

### A3. CPC18 — Calibration and full raw data
- **URLs / DOIs:**
  - Calibration set: https://zenodo.org/records/845873 — `10.5281/zenodo.845873` (510,750 choices, 45 MB CSV)
  - Full raw data: https://zenodo.org/records/2571510 — `10.5281/zenodo.2571510` (62 MB CSV, calibration + test sets)
- **Citation:** Plonsky, Erev & Ert.
- **License:** **CC-BY-4.0** (both records, verified).
- **Size:** Calibration: **510,750 consequential choices**; full raw adds the competition test set.

## C. Ranked shortlist — 4 most usable

Ranked on (1) licence permissiveness, (2) direct downloadability, (3) JDM relevance to choice/confidence/RT simulation, (4) novelty headroom.

1. **CPC18 full raw data (Zenodo `2571510` + calibration `845873`) — CC-BY-4.0.**
   Direct 45–62 MB CSVs, documented variables including **choice, RT (subset), payoffs, ambiguity, correlation**, 510k+ consequential choices. Strongest benchmark-grade substrate for validating a stochastic choice simulation; combine with **CPC2015 (`321652`)** for a 330k-choice hold-out with higher novelty.

2. **The Confidence Database (OSF `s46pr`) — CC0.**
   The most permissive licence here (public-domain dedication), ~4M trials / 8,700+ participants / 360 files, trial-level **confidence + accuracy + task parameters (+ RT in many studies)**. Best for a large secondary analysis on judgement/confidence; novelty comes from the specific question, not the data.

3. **ITC Database (OSF `3wsae`) — CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0.**
   462 MB single CSV of **choice + response-time** data in intertemporal choice; newly released descriptor → **highest novelty headroom**. NC clause excludes commercial use only. Ideal for validating a simulation that predicts *both* choice and RT.

4. **CRT-V (OSF `xehbv`, Zenodo `22916374`) — CC-BY-4.0.** (tie with Many Labs 3, `ct89g`, CC-BY-4.0)
   8 studies with individual-difference measures (reflection, numeracy-adjacent, sociodemographics); clean, tiny, permissively licensed, and useful as a predictor/covariate for JDM simulation parameters and secondary individual-difference analyses.
   - *Alternative #4 if a large replication sample is preferred:* **Many Labs 3 (`ct89g`, CC-BY-4.0)**, though its core JDM relevance is weaker.

**Best single combination for the two stated goals:** use **CPC18 + CPC2015** to validate the simulation (choice/RT/risk/ambiguity/experience), and **Confidence Database** for the secondary JDM analysis (confidence/accuracy). Add **ITC Database** if intertemporal choice is in scope, or **CRT-V** if individual differences are.
